rows.explanation: It has disciples strengthened, exhorted to continue in faith, and told that tribulation must be endured to enter God's kingdom.
It calls believers to hold fast their confession of faith without wavering because God is faithful.
It commands believers to consider one another in order to spur one another to love and good works.
It makes gathering and mutual exhortation the response to the approaching Day.
It commands daily mutual exhortation so that none is hardened by sin's deceitfulness.
It links sharing in Christ with holding the initial confidence steadfast to the end.
It identifies the saints by patience, obedience to God's commandments, and the faith of Jesus.
It commends works, love, service, faith, and patience together.
It joins works, labor, and patience with testing false apostles rather than accepting false claims.
It joins a work of faith with steadfastness of hope.
It tells the community to warn the disorderly, comfort the fainthearted, support the weak, and be patient toward all.
It praises patience and faith amid persecutions and tribulations that believers endure.
It asks whether a claimed faith lacking works can save.
It says faith works together with works and is completed by works.
It explicitly says a person is justified by works and not by faith only.
It requires love not merely in speech but in deed and truth.
It joins faith in Jesus' name with loving one another.
It tells those who have believed God to be careful to maintain good works.
It presents faith as active through love.
It promises eternal life to those who patiently continue in well doing.
It tells believers to inherit the promise through faith and patience.
It says patience is needed after doing God's will in order to receive the promise.
It tells believers not to grow weary in doing good because they will reap in due season.
It joins steadfastness with abundant work and says such labor is not vain in the Lord.
It places righteousness, faith, love, patience, and meekness together as things to pursue.
It directs believers to add virtue and knowledge to faith.
It places patience in the sequence of qualities added to faith.
It joins obeying truth with sincere brotherly love and commands mutual love.
It commends patiently enduring suffering that comes from doing good.
It links persevering in sound teaching with salvation for both teacher and hearers.
It commands proclamation, correction, and exhortation with all longsuffering and doctrine.
It joins holding the faithful word with exhorting by sound doctrine and refuting opponents.
It describes believers as full of goodness and knowledge and able to admonish one another.
It commands the word of Christ to dwell richly among believers as they teach and admonish one another.
It calls believers to speak truth in love so that the body may grow.
It requires each person to speak truth with a neighbor because believers are members of one another.
It commands spiritually mature believers to restore a fallen brother gently while watching themselves.
It commands believers to bear one another's burdens.
It requires correction of a disobedient person as a brother rather than treatment as an enemy.
It describes a brother wandering from truth and another person turning him back.
It says that turning a sinner back saves a soul from death and covers many sins.
It describes those who keep the received word in a good heart and bear fruit with patience.
It promises salvation to the one who endures to the end.
It promises salvation to the one who endures to the end amid hatred for Jesus' name.
It connects patience with gaining or preserving one's life.
It denies kingdom entry to mere verbal profession and requires doing the Father's will.
It commands direct correction of a brother who sins, aiming to gain the brother back.
It promises that the believer will not perish but have everlasting life.
It joins doing truth with deeds shown to have been wrought in God.
It makes continuing in Jesus' word the mark of being his true disciple.
It calls believers to stand firm in one spirit and strive together for the faith of the gospel.
It promises protection to those who have kept Christ's word of patience.
It names the patience and faith of the saints together.
It contrasts drawing back to perdition with believing to the saving of the soul.
It calls believers fellow workers for the truth through receiving and supporting its servants.
It commands rebuking a neighbor rather than hating silently and sharing in the neighbor's sin.
It describes the accepted person as walking uprightly, working righteousness, and speaking truth in the heart.
It joins trusting the LORD with doing good.
It welcomes the righteous person's corrective rebuke as a kindness rather than rejecting it.
It commands speaking truth to one's neighbor and giving judgments of truth and peace.
It says that one who practices God's judgments and deals truly is just and shall surely live.
It promises life rather than death to the wicked person who turns, keeps God's statutes, and does what is lawful and right.
It says that the just person shall live by faith.
It makes being established depend on believing.
It says that the work of righteousness produces peace, quietness, and assurance.
It describes truth in the teacher's mouth, walking in peace and equity, and turning many from iniquity.
It joins trust in God amid mortal suffering with maintaining one's ways before him.
It honors those who turn many toward righteousness.
It contrasts the just, who walk in the LORD's right ways, with transgressors, who fall in them.
It joins loving, obeying, and cleaving to the LORD with life itself.
It has Abraham command his household to keep the LORD's way by doing justice and judgment.
It denies that salvation comes from righteous works done by people and attributes salvation to divine mercy.
It says salvation is not of works so that no one may boast.
It counts faith as righteousness for the one who does not work.
It says that a person is justified by faith apart from deeds of the law.
It repeatedly denies justification by works of the law and grounds it in faith in Christ.
It predicts that people will refuse to endure sound doctrine, reversing endurance in truth.
It says that people will turn their ears from truth to fables.
It praises bearing, patience, labor for Christ's name, and not fainting.
It joins growing faith with love that believers show toward one another.
It culminates the sequence added to faith in brotherly kindness and love.
It commands resistance steadfast in faith while recognizing shared suffering among fellow believers.
It directs older men to be sound in faith, love, and patience.
It makes mutual moral restoration an act requiring gentleness and self-watchfulness.
It turns admonition into a fraternal rather than hostile act.
It says that the righteous hold on their way and those with clean hands grow stronger.
It tells people who know righteousness and bear God's law in their hearts not to fear human reproach.
It says Abram believed the LORD and that this was counted to him as righteousness.
It commands God's words to be diligently taught and continually spoken to the next generation.
It calls God's command not vain but the people's life.
It commands waiting for the LORD with courage and a strengthened heart.
It joins waiting for the LORD and keeping his way with eventual inheritance.
It forbids withholding good when it is due to another person and lies within one's power.
It says righteousness delivers from death when riches cannot.
It joins speaking truth with showing forth righteousness.
It warns that the simple believe every word while the prudent examine their path.
It presents companionship as the means by which one person lifts another after a fall.
It pictures joined persons as a threefold cord that is not quickly broken.
It opens the gate to a righteous nation that keeps truth.
It promises perfect peace to the person whose mind is stayed on God because that person trusts him.
It says that the one who believes will not act in panic.
It promises renewed strength to those who wait on the LORD.
It calls the person blessed whose trust and hope are in the LORD.
It calls it good to wait quietly for the LORD's salvation.
It uses sowing righteousness and reaping mercy to command a renewed seeking of the LORD.
It calls the LORD a stronghold in trouble and says that he knows those who trust him.
It commands waiting for the appointed vision because it will surely come.
It compares hearing and doing Jesus' words to building a house upon rock.
It depicts the house founded on rock as standing through flood, wind, and rain.
It names God's word as truth that sanctifies.
It has Barnabas exhort believers to cleave to the Lord with purpose of heart.
It describes the word of grace as able to build believers up and give them an inheritance.
It makes waiting with patience the response to hope for what is not yet seen.
It promises reward for work that remains after testing.
It warns that a person's burned work brings loss even though the person may be saved.
It promises that God will not allow temptation beyond believers' ability and will provide a way of endurance.
It says believers are created in Christ for good works prepared for them to walk in.
It pictures the joined and supplied body growing as every part does its work in love.
It joins standing firm with truth and righteousness.
It presents faith as a shield against destructive attack.
It commands teaching faithful people who will in turn be able to teach others.
It uses a farmer waiting for precious fruit as an image of patience.
It defines love as walking according to God's commandments.
It commands mercy toward those who doubt.
It says that the works of those who die in the Lord follow them.
It assigns wrath to those who do not obey truth but obey unrighteousness.
It says that people perish because they do not receive the love of truth that would save them.
It calls the professed knower of God who does not keep his commandments a liar in whom truth is absent.
It depicts even Israel's righteousnesses as polluted garments in a confession of uncleanness.
In its idol-making scene, people encourage one another, making reciprocal encouragement serve a false project rather than truth.
It depicts craftsmen strengthening one another to fasten an idol so that it will not move.
It describes people who advance through falsehood and are not valiant for truth.
It portrays justice turned back and truth fallen in the street.
It contrasts mature stability in truth with being tossed about by every wind of teaching.
It compares hearing Jesus' words without doing them to a house built on sand that collapses.
It pictures the righteous person as a well-watered tree yielding enduring fruit.
It compares a person without self-rule to a defenseless city whose walls are broken down.
It says that two are better than one because they receive a good reward for their labor.
It uses abiding in the vine and bearing much fruit as an image of dependent, productive fidelity.
It pictures the community as joined and knit together by joints and bands as it grows from God.
It asks what profit there is in gaining the world while losing one's own soul.
It commands pursuing what is altogether just so that the people may live and inherit the land.
It joins continual attention to God's instruction with doing it and with a prosperous, successful way.
It commands fearing the LORD and serving him in truth with the whole heart.
It joins seeking God's law, doing it, and teaching its statutes and judgments to Israel.
Job receives adversity without charging God foolishly, exemplifying restrained endurance under suffering.
It asks integrity and uprightness to preserve the speaker while he waits for God.
It links the preservation of life with keeping the tongue from evil and the lips from deceit.
It commands departing from evil, doing good, seeking peace, and pursuing it.
It makes receiving correction a path of life and rejecting reproof a way of error.
It depicts reciprocal formation as iron sharpening iron.
It describes the secure person through righteous walking, upright speech, rejection of unjust gain, and refusal of evil.
It promises a defensible refuge and secure provision to the righteous person just described.
It commands strengthening weak hands and confirming feeble knees.
It commands telling fearful hearts to be strong and not fear because God will come to save.
It joins keeping justice and doing righteousness with the nearness of God's salvation.
It requires amended conduct and true justice between one person and another.
It promises continued dwelling in the land after the preceding conditions of justice and repentance.
It commands seeking good rather than evil in order to live.
It commands loving good, hating evil, and establishing justice.
It summarizes the required life as doing justly, loving mercy, and walking humbly with God.
It makes Nineveh's turning from evil works the occasion for its escape from announced destruction.
It commands true judgment, mercy, and compassion between persons.
It describes the good ground as receiving the word with understanding and bearing fruit.
It compares coming to Jesus, hearing his words, and doing them to building a house.
It depicts that doer as building deeply on rock so that flood cannot shake the house.
Jesus prays that Peter's faith will not fail and charges him, once restored, to strengthen his brethren.
It promises that the one who hears Christ's word and believes has passed from death to life.
It calls belief in the one sent by God the work God requires.
It depicts prophets exhorting and confirming the brethren with many words.
It joins repentance, turning to God, and works fitting for repentance.
It says that doers of the law, rather than hearers only, will be justified.
It joins walking worthily with being fruitful in every good work and increasing in knowledge of God.
It connects divine strength with patience and longsuffering.
It records exhorting, comforting, and charging believers to walk worthily of God and his kingdom.
It commands believers not to grow weary in well doing.
It joins doctrine, faith, longsuffering, love, patience, and persecution in a single faithful pattern.
It commands laboring to enter God's rest rather than falling through unbelief.
It says that the testing of faith produces patience.
It commands patience to complete its work so that believers may become mature and whole.
It commands being doers of the word rather than hearers who deceive themselves.
It promises blessing to the person who continues in the perfect law and acts as a doer.
It joins suffering according to God's will with committing one's soul to God while continuing in well doing.
It makes keeping God's commandments the evidence of knowing him.
It commands faithfulness unto death and promises the crown of life.
It commends works, keeping Christ's word, and not denying his name.
It gives access to the tree of life and the city gates to those who do God's commandments.
It depicts a person with no root who endures only briefly and falls away when tribulation comes.
It depicts one who hears but does not do as a house without a foundation that is destroyed.
It portrays people hating the reprover and abhorring the one who speaks uprightly.
It calls a claim of fellowship false when it is joined to walking in darkness rather than doing truth.
It presents trust under God's wings as refuge and grounds for a full divine reward.
It joins walking in God's ways and keeping his commands with prospering in one's course.
It commands knowing and serving God with a whole heart and willing mind while warning against forsaking him.
It depicts God's law being read distinctly, explained, and made understandable to the people.
It pictures mercy and truth meeting together and righteousness and peace embracing.
It pictures truth springing from the earth while righteousness looks down from heaven.
It promises great peace and stability to those who love God's law.
It compares those who trust in the LORD to Mount Zion, which cannot be moved and abides forever.
It celebrates brothers dwelling together in unity.
It commands mercy and truth to be bound upon the person and written on the heart.
It pictures the fruit of the righteous as a tree of life and links wisdom with winning souls.
It defines strength as ruling one's spirit and being slow to anger.
It depicts steadfast love and brotherhood in adversity.
It commands receiving counsel and instruction in order to become wise in one's latter end.
It commands waiting for the LORD rather than retaliating and promises his saving help.
It says doing justice and judgment is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.
It depicts the righteous person rising again after repeated falls.
It calls a patient spirit better than a proud spirit.
It says the LORD is good to the person who waits for him and seeks him.
It makes warning the wicked a means by which the watchman delivers his own soul.
It calls for seeking the LORD, righteousness, and meekness in hope of shelter on the day of anger.
It commands love for truth and peace.
It joins doing God's commands with teaching them to others.
It contrasts everlasting punishment with everlasting life for the righteous in the preceding judgment scene.
It blesses those who hear God's word and keep it.
It makes keeping Christ's commandments the expression of love for him.
It speaks of fruit that remains rather than fruit that passes away.
It says tribulation produces patience.
It says patience produces tested character and hope.
It combines hope, patience in tribulation, and steadfast prayer.
It commands overcoming evil with good.
It commands the strong to bear the infirmities of the weak rather than please themselves.
It describes love as rejoicing with truth rather than in iniquity.
It describes love as bearing and enduring all things.
It commands watchfulness, standing fast in faith, courage, and strength.
It says that believers stand by faith.
It joins the word of truth with the armor of righteousness.
It commands speech that builds others up and gives grace to hearers.
It joins goodness, righteousness, and truth as the fruit of the Spirit.
It commands believers to work out their salvation with reverence and seriousness.
It commands doing what has been learned, received, heard, and seen in faithful teaching.
It commands standing firm and holding to received teaching.
It prays that believers' hearts will be directed into God's love and Christ's patient waiting.
It joins sincere faith with a pure heart, good conscience, and love as the aim of instruction.
It commands fighting the good fight of faith and laying hold on eternal life.
It commands continuing in the teachings one has learned and become convinced of.
It commands a pattern of good works and doctrine marked by integrity and incorruptibility.
It directs believers to maintain good works so that they will not be unfruitful.
It makes holding confidence and hope firm to the end the condition of being Christ's house.
It commands laying aside entangling sin and running the appointed race with patience.
It commands doing good and sharing with others as sacrifices pleasing to God.
It promises the crown of life to the person who endures temptation.
It pictures the fruit of righteousness as sown in peace by peacemakers.
It presents the prophets as examples of suffering and patience.
It calls Job's endurance blessed and points to the Lord's compassionate outcome.
It commands testing spiritual claims rather than believing every spirit.
It defines love for God as keeping his commandments.
It makes faith the victory that overcomes the world.
It rejoices that believers testify to and walk in truth.
It commands believers to build themselves up in their most holy faith.
It commands rescuing others by pulling them from the fire.
It commands holding fast what believers have until Christ comes.
It forbids spreading a false report or joining the wicked as a false witness.
It forbids following a crowd into evil or perverting justice by one's testimony.
It indicts the land for lacking truth, mercy, and knowledge of God.
It describes people suppressing truth through unrighteousness.
It says that people exchanged God's truth for a lie and served the creature instead of the Creator.
It depicts putting away faith and a good conscience as a shipwreck of faith.
It describes people who err concerning truth and overthrow others' faith.
It says that false teachers cause the way of truth to be evil spoken of.
It rebukes tolerating a false teacher who instructs and seduces Christ's servants.
